schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE HEARTBEAT — the most basic mechanism in Cairn: ONE daemon that provides a pulse, and nothing more. It does not execute, resolve, schedule, route, or write any device's state. On each `beat(now, context)` it pulses the SHIM of every subscribed device, in subscription order. Handling a pulse — evaluating the device's PROBES (each trigger where its data is owned, Law 6), firing the due ones by poking the bus — lives in the shim (`cairn/tools/base/shim.py`), NOT here and not in the device body. The ground loop only beats. It also PUBLISHES ITS ROSTER (`roster()`, web-server child c) at all times — the devices it beats to, in order, each with live wakefulness — as the authoritative nav for the web presentation surface; no new owner and no new state, the roster IS the subscription list this device already owns (Law 6). THE ONE WRITE IT OWNS (ticket ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness, 2026-08-09): a resident loop constructed with its instance home touches `~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/liveness.json` atomically on every beat — last-run, state, pid — and `liveness.read_liveness(now)` answers LIVE/DEAD at the ruled 5s threshold (Akien 2026-07-31), that number's ONE address. Liveness is this device's owned fact, READ, never scanned from the process table; a crashed loop leaves the file behind but stops advancing the stamp — that is the whole detector. THE DOOR GUARDS ITSELF (ticket an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once, 2026-08-09): the runner claims the singleton atomically before constructing the device — `guard.claim_singleton`, an flock held for the process's whole life on `<instance>/run.lock` (kernel-released on death, so a corpse leaves no stale claim), because read-then-act is not atomic and two entry points could both read DEAD in one window. Any entry point gains the only-once guarantee by spawning `python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop` — a CALL, not a policy (Law 1/6); a losing launch reads the RECORD to say what is running and exits 3, distinct from a crash. THE FACE (ticket the-ground-loop-pane-shows-its-state, 2026-08-09): the loop gets a device page the way every device does — `declared_panes()` offers one LIVENESS pane whose data IS `read_liveness(now)` plus a single 'reports' label naming the resident record (render, never derive; the 5s stays at its one address), and `GroundLoopShim` fronts the HANDED chassis (constructor injection — never a lazy second loop) so the listener subscribes the heartbeat's own shim to the heartbeat: ground_loop rides its own roster, and the nav carries it because the roster does. The self-subscription is inert under the beat (no probes declared). Never a route, a port, or a server of its own — one web server, surfaces in the shim. IT ALSO KNOWS ITS OWN AGE (ticket the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device, 2026-08-14). A daemon that outlives a code change holds modules that no longer match their files, so every probe it loads binds classes its own frame no longer holds — and the import failures that follow are evidence about the PROCESS while naming the DEVICE. Measured: for 29 hours fifteen devices were benched under their own names and twenty-two probes went dark, self-sealingly, because a benched device stops being re-scanned and an outage that stops recurring reads exactly like one that ended. On the probe-load failure path ONLY — a healthy pass never asks — `staleness.module_drift()` answers whether a module THIS PROCESS HOLDS has stopped matching its file, by two evidences that name no symbol: VANISHED (the file is no longer at that address) and REWRITTEN (the source mtime disagrees with the mtime recorded in the bytecode this process loaded). When it does, NOBODY is benched, the devices keep their shims and the probes in their folders that still load keep firing, and ONE trouble is raised against the loop itself under an identity deliberately outside TROUBLE_PREFIX — because `_refresh_bench` recovers a device name by stripping that prefix, so a self-trouble inside it would bench a phantom device forever. THE SECOND REGISTRATION SURFACE (ticket the-pulse-file-is-the-subscription, 2026-08-15): PRESENCE IS THE SUBSCRIPTION. Any component gets ground-loop service by placing `groundloop/pulse.py` at its own address — class level (beside its code) or instance level (under `~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/`); both present means BOTH fire, because the unit is the FILE. Each beat the loop diffs found-vs-known (`PulseCache` in discovery.py): a new file is imported once under a synthetic `cairn._pulse.*` name (mtime-cached, a raising file lands as a complete refusal dict retried only when its mtime changes); a vanished file is dropped AND evicted from sys.modules the same pass — identity is path+mtime, so an in-place edit is remove+add in one beat. FIRING STAYS IN THE SHIM: the module's `on_pulse(now, context)` hook is served by BaseShim._serve_pulses inside the shim's own on_pulse, never by the loop (the loop only beats, still). A pulse-only device gets a DiscoveredShim; the roster of live pulse services and the bounded event ring ride state() into liveness.json — no new durable record. Nobody registers, nobody restarts, and the loop holds nothing that can go stale: the disk is the roster. Watched live by probes/pulse_service_within_a_beat.py. AND IT RESTARTS ITSELF (ticket a-stale-loop-restarts-itself, 2026-08-19). When the staleness predicate sets `stale` True, the runner exits cleanly — the launcher respawns a fresh process, and the trouble ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges becomes transient instead of standing. TWO COMMAND FLAGS in instance-space control the behavior, using Akien's presence-based architecture: a permanent MENU at `<instance>/flags/` (ls shows what is available) and active SIGNALS as zero-byte copies in the instance folder. Touch to signal, rm to clear — the menu never empties because the signal is a copy, not a move. `COMMAND_EXIT.flag` shuts down the loop on the next beat. `COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag` suppresses the drift-triggered exit during development. The runner checks the signal folder with two stat calls per beat — the flag check IS the poll, no inotify, no daemon. Proved: proofs/test_stale_restart.py (7 teeth: stale property, command exit, staleness-triggered exit, suppression by do-not-restart, flags menu creation, healthy-no-exit). Watched live by probes/a_stale_loop_restarts_itself.py.
why: A single daemon structure that everyone else hangs their own handlers on — so no device runs a bespoke loop or daemon of its own (the UU disease: dozens of independent daemons rotting silently). One heartbeat; every device's shim hangs its probes on it. The decisive property, and the reason the ground loop stays this small: the PROBE IS THE SAME UNIT whether it fires on a scheduled cadence or on a device's own internal trigger — same shape, same firing path in the shim, only the owner and location of its data differ. Keeping the ground loop to just-the-beat is what makes that sameness hold. The heartbeat holds NO runtime state of its own; all durable state lives in db_domain, reached by the devices the shim wakes.
invoke: Construct: `gl = GroundLoopDevice()` (anonymous, no device space — what proofs build) or `GroundLoopDevice(liveness_home=liveness.instance_home())` (the resident singleton — every beat touches its record). A device subscribes its shim: `gl.subscribe(shim)` (idempotent by device_id; only a shim — device_id + on_pulse — may subscribe). Beat: `gl.beat(now, context)` pulses every subscribed shim once and returns a legible beat-record. `now` is passed explicitly, so the pulse is provable without a clock. Run resident: `python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop` (the thin wall-clock backing, ruled 1s cadence, SIGTERM-clean; SELF-GUARDING — a second launch refuses with exit 3, naming what the record said, so spawning it is always safe). Ask liveness: `liveness.read_liveness(now)` → {verdict LIVE|DEAD, record, age_s}. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_ground_loop.py` (exit 0 = green).
entry: FRESH design to Form v0. The mechanism is Cairn's own: one daemon, one beat, firing-in-the-shim. No mechanism grafted.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (a) PARTLY LANDED (ticket the-pulse-file-is-the-subscription): subscription by a file in the device's own folder tree now EXISTS — groundloop/pulse.py at class or instance level is found each beat, activated on presence, unloaded on absence. Residue: probe-carrying devices still ride the probes/ discovery roster in-process, and devices as separate OS processes remain the unbuilt half of this edge

(b) LANDED (ticket ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness): the wall-clock daemon now exists as __main__.py — still the thin wrapper the pulse physics stays provable without. Residue: the runner is session-mortal; the host-seam unit file keeping it alive across sessions is the standing IOU, its own ticket when cast
(c) subscribing real device shims at runner launch — the record needed a beating loop, not a populated roster; subscription grows against need (the start-guard and pane siblings come first)

(d) THE BENCH IS STICKY BY DESIGN AND HAS NO CLI DOOR — clearing is the recipient's act (Law 6) and a restart does not un-bench, so the correct order after any bench is restart, verify through the loop's own discover(), THEN clear. Today the clear is only reachable from Python (TroubleDevice.clear); the missing `cairn trouble clear` door is older than the staleness ticket and separately owed. Residue after that ticket: nothing yet reds a bench ticket that has outlived its cause, which is what probes/loop_not_stale.py watches for rather than prevents.
gates: proof gate (tester) — proofs/test_ground_loop.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) the ground loop does MORE than beat — if it resolves a method, runs a probe, writes state, or routes a poke itself, it has re-absorbed the shim's role (the goof); (2) firing lives anywhere but the shim — a device that must implement its own loop to get its probes fired breaks 'built into all devices'; (3) `subscribe` accepts a non-shim (no on_pulse), or double-subscribes the same device_id; (4) a probe fired on a cadence differs in shape or handling from one fired on a device's own internal trigger (the sameness is the whole point); (5) the heartbeat holds runtime state of its own instead of only beating (durable state is db_domain's, reached by the woken devices) — with the ONE ruled exception of its own liveness record in its own device space (Law 6: its own fact; ticket ground-loop-writes-its-own-liveness), whose own reds are: the stamp not advancing while the loop runs, advancing while it does not, a reader ever seeing a torn record, or the 5s threshold gaining a second class-space address; (6) the only-once guarantee breaking (ticket an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once): two simultaneous launches yielding two loops, a loser blocking instead of refusing loudly, a dead winner's claim needing a hand to break, or the guard deciding from the process table instead of the flock + record; (7) THE LOOP BLAMES A DEVICE FOR ITS OWN AGE — a device benched while its probe folder imports cleanly under a fresh discover(), which is the exact signature of the 29-hour outage; or the converse, a genuinely broken device NOT benched while this process holds no drifted module, which would trade one silent failure for another. The pair must prove APART on the same fixture (proofs/test_discovery.py), or the predicate is not what decides. Also red: the staleness question answered from the TREE rather than from what this process HOLDS — 'newest mtime in the tree > process start' was MEASURED FALSE against the live healthy loop during that ticket's survey and survives only as labelled payload in `staleness.diagnostics`, never as the test; a module the predicate cannot judge reported as fresh rather than UNDECIDABLE (absence of evidence is not evidence of freshness, Law 9); and the predicate special-casing the two faces seen in 2026-08 by symbol name or error text, since the next rename would produce a third face and the loop would blame a device again. NOTE ON CLAUSE (5): the predicate holds NO state — it is recomputed from sys.modules and disk on the failure path, and the per-module load times that would be the more direct comparison were REFUSED for exactly that reason. CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (ticket staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk): this note used to end 'the bytecode header already carries the answer for free', and that sentence was measured FALSE. A .pyc is a SHARED artifact, so the header's mtime and the source's mtime are BOTH on disk and neither term contains the asker — any second interpreter importing the module repairs the evidence without repairing this process. Measured: an ordinary proof run in the same tree refreshed the header, the predicate answered empty, and the loop benched an innocent device at 03:44Z. What replaces it holds the asker in it — the code objects THIS PROCESS holds against a fresh compile of the file — so it still needs no clock and no stored load times, and clause (5) stands for the same reason by a mechanism that does not depend on who else has run. The retired comparison survives as labelled payload beside tree_newer_than_process, in staleness.diagnostics' not_the_predicate list. AND THE COVERAGE IS REPORTED WITH THE VERDICT: findings alone cannot separate 'compared 398 objects, none disagreed' from 'could compare nothing', because a clean process yields an empty list either way — measured at 0 undecidable over a process where 181 objects were unreachable.
how_it_learns: The heartbeat itself does not learn — it is the floor everything beats on (like the core values, a deliberate terminal simplicity). Learning happens in the PROBES the shims hang on it: each probe is a handler whose firing leaves evidence on the bus. The lesson this component itself carries is a specimen of learning-its-gates: collapsing the heartbeat, the executor, and the scheduler into one device was caught by Akien at n=1 and corrected before it hardened — the ground loop learned to be smaller (its `run_driver` and registry were deleted, not patched). Its horizon: whether one heartbeat daemon + shim-fired probes covers a scheduled cadence AND a device's own internal triggers with the SAME probe — measured as more real probes land (the system device's threshold pokes are the first). ONE MORE LESSON, and it is about the reader rather than the code: this device's own trouble list was loud, correctly recorded, and pointed at the wrong party for 29 hours, and every session — including two of mine — read it at session open and walked past it. Being pointed at the wrong party is what made it quiet. That is why the fix is not a better error string: probes/loop_not_stale.py fires on the RELATION (benched AND imports cleanly), which is the reading no human took because it needed the second measurement run against the first.

build order: db domain → ground loop → … (MAP.md:892)
owner: CC owns the ground_loop code + its proofs and gates writes to them. The heartbeat is the shared substrate every device's shim depends on; the probes hung on it are owned by their own devices (class-space declarations), and any durable state they touch is owned through db_domain.
proof: proofs/test_ground_loop.py — the beat pulses every subscribed shim in order and leaves a beat-record; the firing is the shim's (a due probe pokes the bus, the heartbeat pokes nothing, an idle beat pokes nobody); subscribe is idempotent + refuses a non-shim; one shim raising cannot stop the beat (CP2); the executor goof is gone (no run_driver/registry); device-hood + Form v0 #2 order; and the ROSTER is the nav (web-server child c) — published at all times, in order, with live wakefulness, DATA the web server renders. Composes the real BaseShim + Probe + a spy bus, so it proves the beat → pulse → fire chain WITHOUT a DB. Green bare (python3) and under the tester. proofs/test_staleness.py — the predicate's own teeth, WRITTEN BEFORE IT EXISTED: an edit to a file this process never imported stays green, a module loaded late from a newly written file stays green (the false positive found by reproduction, not reasoning), a genuinely drifted module and a module whose file moved away both go red, a module with no timestamped bytecode reads UNDECIDABLE rather than green, a module that never came from a file at all is not drift (the `<stdin>` false positive, found by aiming the finished predicate at the real world), and n=1 against the ACTUAL outage — the pre-move address git says commit ba50814 deleted. The greens are measured on a package with NO staleness present, because a green measured on an already-stale process proves nothing. proofs/test_discovery.py carries the pair that must prove apart plus the phantom-bench trap. Green bare (python3) and under the tester. proofs/test_loop_not_stale.py — the PROBE's own teeth, and this file exists because the probe shipped with none: it was discovered, loaded and berthed while its every-beat path raised AttributeError on a name that does not exist, and a 107-green suite said nothing because no proof ever CALLED it. A watch that cannot run is a watch that is off, which is this device's own failure mode one level up. Its first tooth takes no fixture at all — it calls the trigger the way the beat calls it — and the rest bite on: a CLEARED bench ticket counted as a bench (the cheap and expensive halves once held disagreeing definitions of 'benched', disagreeing exactly in the state that follows acting on this probe's advice), firing on a device that is genuinely broken, clearing on silence from either side, and the diagnosis ORDER surviving in the carry. Both shipped defects were falsified against restored-broken copies rather than assumed caught. Green bare (python3) and under the tester.
provenance: Born 2026-07-18 as the fifth spine step, first built as a generic driver-executor (cairn `584aa74`). Same day (evening), reworked to the heartbeat after the design conversation with Akien restored the lost property — a probe is the same unit whether fired on a cadence or on a device's own trigger — and located the firing in the shim. The rework SIMPLIFIES: the central scheduler (system_rackmount's scheduler service) dissolves, `run_driver` + the method-registry strip away, and one universal mechanism replaces three. Built third in the rework (after the bus and the base's probe+shim, both of which it pulses onto). Then the spine resumes (MAP.md:892): inference domain → web server.
